analysis: The trial succeeded with host-evaluated macro validation HR@10 of 0.535, exceeding the supplied 0.505 baseline by 0.030. Category HR@10 was 0.570 for Movies_and_TV, 0.535 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.355 for Electronics, and 0.680 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics remains the weakest category. These results support unordered purchase-history reconstruction as a useful approach, but do not establish that ignoring order caused the improvement. Allocated GPU time was 104.27 seconds; no test results were available.
code_summary: Trains a separate multinomial VAE for each of four dataset routes. Binary, deduplicated histories enter a sparse, length-normalized EmbeddingBag encoder with 50% input dropout, a 256-unit hidden layer, and a 64-dimensional Gaussian latent representation. A nonlinear decoder reconstructs purchases across the full catalog using multinomial loss plus an annealed KL penalty capped at 0.2. Adam trains the models; local validation HR@10 selects checkpoints, with NDCG@10 breaking ties and early stopping after 25 epochs without improvement. The generated predictor loads matching category checkpoints and scores candidates using the deterministic posterior mean. Training reads only supplied training and validation splits, retains GAGC_DATA_DIR, and saves artifacts under the trial's working directory.
